en: The Legend of the Elder Sayanadāyaka Upāli Chapter, Number 7 [Verse 1] In the city of Bandhumatī, I was born as a wealthy householder; I possessed great riches and grain, and I was honored by many people. [Verse 2] At that time, the Teacher, the Great Sage, the Fully Enlightened One, the Buddha, appeared in the world, bringing light to the world of men. [Verse 3] Having heard that the Teacher had arrived at Bandhumatī, I went to the presence of the Buddha, desiring to see him. [Verse 4] Having approached the Teacher, I paid homage with my head to his feet; then I sat down to one side, having honored the Blessed One. [Verse 5] Then the Teacher, the Great Sage, knowing my intention, preached the Dhamma to me, which is excellent in the beginning, the middle, and the end. [Verse 6] Having heard the Dhamma from the Teacher, I was filled with joy; I then offered a bed to the Teacher, the Fully Enlightened One. [Verse 7] Having made that offering to the Teacher, the Fully Enlightened One, I passed away from that human existence and was reborn in heaven. [Verse 8] For eighty-four thousand aeons, I dwelt in the realm of the gods; having exhausted that kamma, I have now attained this human state. [Verse 9] I am well-born, handsome, and endowed with great wealth; I possess a vast retinue, and I am honored by many people. [Verse 10] Because of that gift of a bed to the Teacher, the Fully Enlightened One, I have obtained this fruit of merit, which is most excellent. [Verse 11] May I also attain the supreme, unsurpassed enlightenment; may I become a teacher of devas and humans, just like the Buddha. [Verse 12] May I be a refuge for the world, including the devas; may I be a protector for those who are without protection. [Verse 13] May I be a shelter for those who are without shelter; may I be a lamp for those who are without a lamp. [Verse 14] May I be a leader for those who are without a leader; may I be a guide for those who are lost in the wilderness. [Verse 15] May I be a boat for those who are without a boat; may I be a ford for those who are without a ford. [Verse 16] May I be an island for those who are without an island; may I be a light for those who are in darkness. [Verse 17] May I be a physician for those who are sick; may I be a healer for those who suffer from disease. [Verse 18] May I be a mother and a father to all beings; may I be a friend to all, impartial toward both enemies and kin. [Verse 19] May I be a source of happiness for all living beings; may I bring relief to those who are oppressed by suffering. [Verse 20] May I be a vessel of merit for the world; may I be a field of merit for all who seek it. [Verse 21] May I be a treasury of virtue for the world; may I be a storehouse of wisdom for all beings. [Verse 22] May I be a mountain of stability for the world; may I be a tree of compassion for those in need. [Verse 23] May I be a cloud of rain for the thirsty; may I be a wind of liberation for those bound in saṃsāra. [Verse 24] May I be a sun for the dispelling of darkness; may I be a moon for the cooling of the fever of passion. [Verse 25] May I be a thunderbolt for the destruction of Māra; may I be a lion for the subduing of the elephant of defilement. [Verse 26] May I be a peacock for the destruction of the snake of craving; may I be a Garuda for the lifting of the serpent of ignorance. [Verse 27] May I be a lotus for the cleansing of the mud of birth; may I be a jewel for the fulfillment of all desires. [Verse 28] May I be a wish-fulfilling gem for the world; may I be a nectar for the quenching of the thirst of existence. [Verse 29] May I be a bridge for crossing over the ocean of saṃsāra; may I be a path for reaching the city of Nibbāna. [Verse 30] May I be a chariot for the journey to the Deathless; may I be a ship for crossing the river of suffering. [Verse 31] May I be a ladder for ascending to the heights of peace; may I be a staircase for reaching the peak of liberation. [Verse 32] May I be a door for entering the city of safety; may I be a key for opening the gate of the Dhamma. [Verse 33] May I be a torch for lighting the way in the dark; may I be a mirror for seeing the truth of reality. [Verse 34] May I be a drum for proclaiming the victory of the Dhamma; may I be a conch for sounding the call to awakening. [Verse 35] May I be a banner for the victory over Māra; may I be a victory for the conquest of all defilements. [Verse 36] May I be a victory for the defeat of suffering; may I be a triumph for the attainment of Nibbāna. [Verse 37] May I be a victory for the establishment of the Triple Gem; may I be a victory for the preservation of the holy life. [Verse 38] May I be a victory for the protection of the Dhamma; may I be a victory for the guidance of the Sangha. [Verse 39] May I be a victory for the welfare of the world; may I be a victory for the happiness of all beings. [Verse 40] May I be a victory for the cessation of birth; may I be a victory for the end of old age and death. [Verse 41] May I be a victory for the end of sorrow and lamentation; may I be a victory for the end of pain and despair. [Verse 42] May I be a victory for the end of mental distress; may I be a victory for the end of all conditioned things. [Verse 43] May I be a victory for the realization of the Truth; may I be a victory for the attainment of the Path. [Verse 44] May I be a victory for the fruition of the Path; may I be a victory for the attainment of Nibbāna. [Verse 45] May I be a victory for the destruction of the fetters; may I be a victory for the attainment of the fruits of holiness. [Verse 46] May I be a victory for the purification of the mind; may I be a victory for the perfection of wisdom. [Verse 47] May I be a victory for the mastery of the powers; may I be a victory for the attainment of the fearlessnesses. [Verse 48] May I be a victory for the knowledge of the destruction of the taints; may I be a victory for the proclamation of the final Nibbāna. [Verse 49] May I be a victory for the turning of the Wheel of the Dhamma; may I be a victory for the establishment of the Dispensation. [Verse 50] May I be a victory for the preservation of the relics; may I be a victory for the spread of the Teaching throughout the world. [Verse 51] May I be a victory for the honoring of the shrines; may I be a victory for the worship of the Buddhas. [Verse 52] May I be a victory for the recitation of the Suttas; may I be a victory for the study of the Vinaya. [Verse 53] May I be a victory for the exposition of the Abhidhamma; may I be a victory for the preservation of the Three Baskets. [Verse 54] May I be a victory for the practice of meditation; may I be a victory for the attainment of the jhānas. [Verse 55] May I be a victory for the development of the factors of enlightenment; may I be a victory for the cultivation of the Noble Eightfold Path. I gave a bed at the head of the couch.”
the Blessed One accepted that suitable bedding and seating.
the Victor ascended into the air ninety-four aeons ago.
The bed that I gave away—
of that bed I do not know a bad destination;
this is the fruit of the bed.
there was a king named Devasava,
who was endowed with the seven treasures.
A wheel-turning monarch of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Sayanadāyaka recited these verses.
This is the seventh legend of the elder Sayanadāyaka.
